fact_text: For oil producers the oil price is the main swing factor in earnings; a new gas discovery moves the company's value only slightly, according to the analyst.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Analyse Oil & Gas Stocks in Pakistan | Earnings, Reserves & Cash Flow' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: An upstream producer's drilling costs, salaries and other operating costs are largely fixed, so most of any oil price change reaches profit after royalty and levy.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Analyse Oil & Gas Stocks in Pakistan | Earnings, Reserves & Cash Flow' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Gas revenue for upstream producers is set by a regulated price, so it is almost fixed and does not follow global prices, the analyst said.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Analyse Oil & Gas Stocks in Pakistan | Earnings, Reserves & Cash Flow' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The windfall levy applies to oil revenue when the oil price rises above a threshold, and the government takes roughly 40% to 50% of the excess, per the analyst.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Analyse Oil & Gas Stocks in Pakistan | Earnings, Reserves & Cash Flow' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Oil royalty is 12.5%, so a higher oil price also raises the royalty payment, not only the windfall levy.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Analyse Oil & Gas Stocks in Pakistan | Earnings, Reserves & Cash Flow' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: In the analyst's rough example, a 50% oil price rise on about 100 billion of oil sales lifts revenue only to about 125 to 130 after levy and royalty, and profit roughly half the revenue gain.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Analyse Oil & Gas Stocks in Pakistan | Earnings, Reserves & Cash Flow' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: 2P reserves are proven plus probable reserves; estimating them needs surveys and test wells first, which is why companies spend heavily before the figures are firm.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Analyse Oil & Gas Stocks in Pakistan | Earnings, Reserves & Cash Flow' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst treated reserve life of about 10 years or more as comfortable, and a producer below that as one to avoid.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Analyse Oil & Gas Stocks in Pakistan | Earnings, Reserves & Cash Flow' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Mature fields have kept reserve life under about 20 years because operators re-appraise nearby areas and drill new wells, so output is sustained by replacement.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Analyse Oil & Gas Stocks in Pakistan | Earnings, Reserves & Cash Flow' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Offshore blocks typically need five to seven years of survey work before a first well is drilled, so a discovery can be five to ten years away.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Analyse Oil & Gas Stocks in Pakistan | Earnings, Reserves & Cash Flow' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Discoveries are generally not valued until announced, and the analyst said near-term earnings over the next one to three years drive valuations more than distant prospects.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Analyse Oil & Gas Stocks in Pakistan | Earnings, Reserves & Cash Flow' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Oil sales are usually paid in cash, so circular debt builds mainly on gas sales, where payments run late.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Analyse Oil & Gas Stocks in Pakistan | Earnings, Reserves & Cash Flow' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: PPL has a larger gas share than OGDC, which the analyst linked to higher circular-debt exposure for PPL.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Analyse Oil & Gas Stocks in Pakistan | Earnings, Reserves & Cash Flow' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Under the 2012 gas policy, incremental output from existing fields could be sold at a higher two-tier price, and a field already on the 2012 terms could not claim the tier twice.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Analyse Oil & Gas Stocks in Pakistan | Earnings, Reserves & Cash Flow' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The government later applied a newer, higher windfall levy to oil from fields such as the Tal block that had taken the new gas price; operators argued the policy covered only gas, which became a court dispute.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Analyse Oil & Gas Stocks in Pakistan | Earnings, Reserves & Cash Flow' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Operators in a pricing dispute may keep booking revenue at the old price while the case runs, and record any extra amount later if they win.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Analyse Oil & Gas Stocks in Pakistan | Earnings, Reserves & Cash Flow' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst doubted a reported Arabian Sea discovery, calling it an estimate drawn from the basin's age, since no systematic offshore survey had yet been done.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'How to Analyse Oil & Gas Stocks in Pakistan | Earnings, Reserves & Cash Flow' (YouTube transcript, undated)
